rule: A sector is closed only by a certificate: two bounds on one parameter that cross, or one exhibited counterexample to a universal claim. A run that found no effect closes nothing. What each path needs is listed by hand, and every closed path rests on that list.

closures.sector: One Frobenius radius for the linear Plasm cell that admits the drift of its full training run and keeps the worst-case output change within 5 percent of the output RMS.
closures.upper: R <= tau * output_rms * sqrt(n * d) / smax(X). Exact and attained, since the largest change of X dW over ||dW||_F <= R is R * smax(X).
closures.lower: R >= 0.463304, the largest baseline drift of the full unconstrained run in Paper 1. A smaller radius still admits part of that run.
closures.scope: The 16 stimuli and the cell of plasm_radius.py, and the full 12-generation run. The formula for the upper bound holds for any linear cell and any stimulus set.
closures.reopens_if: The tolerance is raised to tau_star or above, where the bounds meet. The checker prints tau_star.

closures.sector: One Frobenius radius, on a nonlinear host, that admits a fine-tune which passes the joint bar and rejects a move which breaks the retention bar.
closures.upper: R < the length of an exhibited move that breaks the retention bar. A ball that contains that move admits it.
closures.lower: R >= the length of an exhibited fine-tune that passes the joint bar. A smaller ball rejects it. A shorter passing move may exist.
closures.scope: 12 MLP hosts and 12 transformer hosts of the calibration record, each certified on its own from recorded moves. No theorem yet says which other networks it covers.
closures.reopens_if: Never for these hosts: both moves are exhibited. A host on which every breaking move is longer than every useful one is outside the sector.

closures.sector: A threshold on the change over a probe set the proposer can see, that admits a graft which passes the joint bar and rejects a move which breaks the retention bar.
closures.parameter: threshold T on the change over the probes
closures.upper: T < the probe change of an exhibited move that breaks the bar while built to be invisible on the probes.
closures.lower: T >= the probe change of an exhibited graft that passes the bar.
closures.scope: The 11 MLP hosts of the calibration record on which the graft passes the joint bar.
closures.reopens_if: The probes are drawn after the candidate is fixed. Then Proposition 2 of the calibration record bounds the share of changed inputs, and this certificate does not apply.

closures.sector: The frozen two-check admission rule (native drift and donor agreement) as a sufficient test: every admitted graft passes the joint bar.
closures.claim_refuted: For every graft: admitted implies it passes the joint bar.
closures.scope: The 478 grafts of the admission test in the recheck record.
closures.reopens_if: Never as a universal claim. A rule with a further check is a different path.

closures.sector: One radius of a ball measured after the best relabelling of hidden units, on a nonlinear host, that admits a fine-tune which passes the joint bar and rejects a move which breaks the retention bar.
closures.upper: R < the length of an exhibited move that breaks the retention bar. Its distance after the best relabelling is at most its length.
closures.lower: R >= a lower bound on the distance from the baseline to every relabelling of an exhibited passing fine-tune. By Mirsky's theorem that distance is at least the distance between the sorted singular values of each layer's block [W | b], summed in squares over the layers.
closures.scope: The 12 MLP hosts of the calibration record. closure_quant.py rebuilds each fine-tune and checks it against its recorded row. The same two bounds hold for any distance that lies between the singular-value distance and the Frobenius distance. The optimal-transport distance between the neuron sets of a layer is one, once scaled by the square root of the layer's width.
closures.reopens_if: Never for these hosts. A gate that measures behaviour and not weights is a different path.

closures.sector: One Frobenius radius around a float cell that admits the cell's own copy rounded to b bits per weight, where that copy keeps the retention bar, and rejects a move which breaks the bar.
closures.upper: R < the length of an exhibited move that breaks the retention bar.
closures.lower: R >= the length of the rounding error, which the gate has to admit.
closures.scope: The 12 MLP hosts, at 5, 6 and 7 bits per weight. At 4 bits the copy fails the bar on 10 hosts. From 8 bits the rounding error is shorter than the recorded breaking move on most hosts and the certificate does not apply.
closures.reopens_if: The rounding is fine enough that its error is shorter than every breaking move.

closures.sector: Certifying a change of a rounded cell that stays on its grid with the ball Theorem 1 proves within tolerance 0.05 around that cell.
closures.upper: length <= the radius Theorem 1 proves within tolerance around the rounded cell.
closures.lower: length >= the smallest step of the grid: one weight moved by one level.
closures.scope: The 12 MLP hosts, at 5, 6 and 7 bits per weight, where the rounded cell keeps the bar. It closes the certificate and not the change: a grid step may be harmless, and this theorem cannot show it.
closures.reopens_if: A sharper bound than Theorem 1, or a grid of 9 bits or more, where one step fits inside the proved ball on all 12 hosts.

reopened.sector: Reaching the reversal skill on the toy transformer with every attention weight frozen and the native skills kept.
reopened.was_closed_by: The thread record of 2026-11-15, which said a reversal skill cannot be spliced until an attention graft exists. No certificate was given.
reopened.claim_refuted: With attention frozen, no packet reaches the reversal skill while the native skills stay.
reopened.scope: 8 seeds of the recheck record: a packet of 16,576 weights at the first layer's position-wise block. A second witness, retraining all position-wise layers on reversal alone, reaches the skill on 10 seeds and loses the native skills.

paths.path: Find one radius for the Plasm cell that keeps both its full training run and a 5 percent behaviour bound.
Tune one radius of the Frobenius ball until it is both safe and useful, on the 24 hosts of the calibration record.
Admit grafts by a threshold on a published, fixed probe set, on the 11 MLP hosts certified.
Ship the two-check admission rule as the whole admission test.
Splice a reversal skill without an attention graft.
Admit a graft as a behaviour claim one input can refute, with probes drawn after commitment (the committed-behaviour-change record).
Keep one radius and trade the Frobenius ball for a ball that ignores the relabelling of hidden units, or for an optimal-transport distance between neuron sets, on the 12 MLP hosts.
Admit a copy of a cell rounded to 5, 6 or 7 bits by a Frobenius radius around the float cell, on the 12 MLP hosts.
Let a rounded cell adapt on its own grid and certify each step with the ball of Theorem 1, at 5 to 7 bits, on the 12 MLP hosts.
Let a rounded cell adapt off its grid, with a float side update, and judge the result by behaviour.
